entries.title: BROOD BUBBLE and URCHIN reef turret, encounter concept
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 side-scrolling arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. Inside a coral-reef tunnel at the heart of a teal-and-violet nebula sea: a BROOD BUBBLE floats center-frame — a translucent wobbling sphere of membranous jelly with a tiny mechanical fish curled asleep inside, its dark spine visible through the shimmering film — while along the sand-stone reef walls a row of URCHIN reef turrets bristle: squat barnacle-domes armored in overlapping charcoal plates, each crowned with a fan of purple spines and a single rotating magenta lens. The MANTA fighter, a flat ray-winged hull of pale mint with a green canopy and amber twin thrusters, banks through the gap on the left, its wake scattering glowing plankton motes. Fired urchin shots leave curling pink trails; the tunnel mouth ahead glows with pale aqua light. Background is a lifted deep-navy to teal gradient, never pure black, layered with drifting wave-like gas rasters. Ultra-detailed, large-format, clean vector shapes with pixel-art texture accents.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, watermark, blurry, pure black background, sea creatures with eyes, cartoon smile, bubbles everywhere
entries.notes: flux.2-dev renders the see-through brood film with the curled fish inside far more reliably than sd3.5. Color reference: nebula teal-violet, sand-stone #f0c890, mint hull #c8e0d0, canopy #40d070, urchin lens #ff5aa0.

entries.title: BROOD BUBBLE and URCHIN reef turret, encounter concept
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, subtle CRT scanline glow, widescreen arcade side-scroller framing. A moment of hazard and harvest in a deep reef corridor: an ruptured BROOD BUBBLE splits down the middle in a slow burst of pink droplets, its mechanical fry spilling out and twitching to life, tiny dark spines unfurling; on the right wall a line of URCHIN reef turrets — barnacle-domes of charcoal plate with purple spine fans and glowing magenta aiming lenses — pivots to track the steel-blue KESTREL dart screaming past at the bottom of the frame, blue hull stripe blazing, cyan canopy catching the reef light, orange engine glow strobing along the tunnel. Wobbling wave rasters of teal gas roll across the corridor like heat-shimmer underwater, sand-stone arches carved with ancient pore-tunnels rise above, and a distant violet nebula heart pulses behind the reef. Lifted deep-navy shadows that never reach pure black, gold point-sparkles drifting where the brood burst caught light. Ultra-detailed, large-format, clean vector shapes with pixel-art texture accents.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d, text, watermark, blurry, pure black, realistic fish, cartoon characters, human divers
entries.notes: Panoramic crop for website zone banners; the rupture action reads best wide. sd3.5 handles the droplet spray cleanly. Keep fry mechanical — dark spines, not organic scales.

entries.title: BROOD BUBBLE and URCHIN reef turret, encounter concept
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, square vertical poster crop, subtle CRT scanline glow. A towering reef column fills a vertical shaft of teal-violet light: stacked URCHIN reef turrets line it like fortified sentries, charcoal barnacle-domes with fanned purple spines and single magenta lenses, their aim-lines converging up the composition. Near the top a swollen BROOD BUBBLE clings to the rock, half-transparent and wobbling, a small mechanical fish curled inside its shimmering membrane, backlit so the film glows pale aqua at the rim. At the very bottom edge, tiny against the reef, the flat winged silhouette of the MANTA fighter climbs into the shaft, twin amber thrusters painting the stone warm, green canopy a bright seed of light. The sea of nebula gas darkens with depth into lifted navy, dusted with glowing plankton and drifting wave rasters. Clean vector shapes with pixel-art texture accents, ultra-detailed, large-format, atmosphere thick but readable.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, logo, watermark, blurry, pure black, submarine cable, wreckage
entries.notes: Vertical "descent shaft" composition sells the nebula's depth. flux.1-dev keeps the stacked turret silhouettes crisp. Color reference: aqua rim glow #6ad8e0 family, spine purple #b84cff, thrusters amber #f89830.

entries.title: In-game sprite sheet: FROTH splitting bubble, four frames on key green
entries.positive: 16-bit SNES-era video game sprite sheet, pixel art style, crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines, saturated limited palette, a regular grid of four equal cells in two rows of two with even gutters, read left to right and top to bottom, one pose per cell in the order listed, the same subject at the same scale, position and light in every cell, on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background, no gradients, no scenery, no text, no labels, no UI. Subject: FROTH — a wobbling translucent pink-white foam-sphere splitting bubble enemy with a darker rim and a bright core. Four frames, side view facing left. The frames in order: intact wobbling sphere; a vertical seam growing down its middle; the sphere pinched deep at the seam; separating into two smaller froth spheres still touching at a thin thread. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the split state changes. Chunky crisp pixels, light dithered shading.
entries.negative: gradient background, text, numbers, labels, photorealistic, 3d render, watermark, soft blur, anti-aliased, realistic fish, pure black background, overlapping sprites, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, background scenery, cast shadow
entries.notes: Froth swarm hazard; the two small spheres of the last frame are separate spawn art drawn from the same body at half size. Froth's pink bubble shots are bullets — procedural, not sprites on this sheet. The GALVANIC MAW's MAW ROCKET torpedo — an open metal fish-jaw nose with a dark throat #080410, stubby fins, a tail flame flickering through four #f89830 states — is its own single-subject strip in this form when the round sheets it. Color reference: froth pink-white #ff5aa0 rim family. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.

entries.title: In-game sprite sheet: BROOD BUBBLE jelly pod, four frames on key green
entries.positive: Retro 16-bit pixel art sprite atlas for a horizontal shoot-'em-up's underwater-reef level, flat solid pure bright green chroma-key sheet, generous margins, evenly spaced, absolutely no text and no annotations. Subject: BROOD BUBBLE — a membranous jelly sphere, translucent violet film glimmering pink, a curled dark mechanical fish-fry visible inside with its charcoal spine showing through the shimmering membrane. Four frames in a regular grid of two rows of two, read left to right and top to bottom: the film intact and taut; wobbling, squashed and stretched; a long seam cracking across it; emptied, the film peeling back from the rim with the fish gone. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the film state changes. Crisp 1-pixel near-black outlines, saturated limited palette of teal, violet, slate and pink, chunky readable small-size forms, dithered highlights only, no anti-aliasing, no scenery behind any sprite.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d, gradients, smooth shading, text, watermark, coral background, water caustics, fish eyes, pure black background, overlapping sprites, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, background scenery, cast shadow
entries.notes: Square texture-page format. sd3.5 keeps the brood sequence legible; check the curled mechanical fry stays readable through the film in every frame and the emptied shell reads as the same pod, not a new object. The hatched fry is a separate small sprite for the next sheet; the pink droplet burst is procedural. Color reference: jelly toward #8a48e8 translucency. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.

entries.title: In-game sprite sheet: URCHIN reef turret, four frames on key green
entries.positive: Pixel art sprite sheet, SNES 16-bit arcade style, flat solid pure bright green chroma-key sheet background, thick even margins, no text, no numbers, no frame borders. A wide horizontal filmstrip of four equal cells in one row, read left to right, one pose per cell, the same subject at the same scale and light in every cell. Subject: URCHIN — a reef-mounted charcoal barnacle turret dome armored in overlapping scales, crowned with a fan of purple crystal spines and a single glowing magenta lens. Four frames, side view facing left. The frames in order: lens aimed straight left; lens tilted up-left; lens tilted down-left; damaged — the same dome aimed left with broken spines and a dimmed lens. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the lens angle and the shell damage change. Crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines on every sprite, limited saturated palette, chunky pixel clusters, light dithering on metal only, classic cartridge-era readability at small scale.
entries.negative: text, labels, UI, gradient background, photorealistic, 3d render, blurry, anti-aliasing, glow bloom, realistic water, watermark, pure black background, overlapping sprites, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, background scenery, cast shadow
entries.notes: Landscape filmstrip layout, best for website sprite-strip displays. flux.1-dev again the steadiest "no-text" producer. The spineless base-only destroyed stump is a follow-up frame; the urchin's curling pink shots are bullets — procedural. Color reference: urchin spine #b84cff, lens #ff3a3a. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.
